correctness.rationale: The gradient of the quartic is e(yzw,xzw,xyw,xyz), so its critical support is exactly six projective coordinate lines. Every vertex has value a≠0, so edge cuts are disjoint. Restricting to each edge gives a monic binary quartic a(u^4+v^4)+βu²v², finite locally free degree 4. A root has order 2 if β≠0, order 4 if β=0. The transverse polar uv coefficient is a unit; formal splitting gives UV+s² or UV+s⁴ (Artin A1 and A3), including zero-wall intersections. Finite singular support implies normal irreducible quartic and K3 resolution. On torus the Gauss map is an involutive cubic Cremona; F after substitution is degree12 primitive irreducible on torus, no coordinate divisor. Independently GF4 count across r=0,1,2,3 gives supports 12,10,8,6 and rank 24; finite computation corroborates but does not establish relative flatness.
residual_risks: Formal splitting in characteristic two uses the nondegenerate transverse polar pair over k[[s]]; individual ADE normal forms apply only where a,e are units.
No assertions about a=0,e=0, or differently scaled integral lattices; finite GF4 data are not the universal proof.
